name: Ozaena
body:
Ozaena
CR 17

This enormous sea creature supports itself on four of its tentacles to walk on land. Its nauseating odor hits you even before you see its maw full of fangs gape.

XP 102,400
N Gargantuan magical beast (aquatic)
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +30; Aura pungent stench (60 ft., DC 29, duration 15 rounds)

DEFENSE

AC 27, touch 11, flat-footed 22 (+5 Dex, +16 natural, -4 size)
hp 262 (21d10+147)
Fort +21, Ref +20, Will +15

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., swim 60 ft., jet 200 ft.
Melee bite +30 (2d8+13, 19-20), 8 tentacles +28 (2d6+13 plus grab)
Space 20 ft., Reach 15 ft. (30 ft. with tentacle)
Special Attacks constrict (tentacle, 2d6+5), ink cloud (60-ft.-radius sphere)

STATISTICS

Str 36, Dex 21, Con 25, Int 16, Wis 22, Cha 3
Base Atk +21; CMB +38 (+42 with grapple); CMD 53 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Acrobatic, Combat Reflexes, Great Fortitude, Improved Critical (bite), Improved Stench, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Multiattack, Power Attack, Pungent Stench
Skills Acrobatics +33 (+41 jump) Escape Artist +36, Perception +30, Stealth +37, Swim +45; Racial Modifiers +10 Escape Artist, +8 Stealth; +8 to Acrobatics checks made to jump
Languages Aboleth, Aquan, Common (cannot speak)
SQ amphibious

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Ink Cloud (Ex)

An ozaena can emit a 60-foot-radius sphere of ink once per minute as a free action. The ink provides total concealment in water and persists for 1 minute.

Jet (Ex)

An ozaena can jet backward once per round as a full-round action, at a speed of 200 feet. It must move in a straight line while jetting and does not provoke attacks of opportunity when it does so.

ECOLOGY

Environment any sea or ocean
Organization solitary
Treasure incidental

The ozaena (“stinking octopus”) is a species of giant octopus of significant intelligence that has developed glands that release a foul oil whose stench both deters predators and handicaps prey. Its fanged maw is studded with teeth, and while it is not venomous its stench debilitates its foes. It resembles a purplish mass while in the water, its roiling tentacles giving off a rancid stench. The skin of the ozaena is thick and wrinkled, like an elephant’s, with colors ranging from deep blues to dark purples and blacks, typically in mottled patterns. The ozaena, like many of its cephalopod cousins, can change its colors to mimic its surroundings, allowing it to hide and ambush prey.

The body of a full grown ozaena can be the size of a bull, with tentacles nearly twice the length of its body.

An ozaena is a cunning predator. The creature can assess situations and triggers that attract the attention of prey and use that knowledge to its advantage. For example, it may use bait to attract prey. This could be plants or other dead creatures set out to attract aquatic prey, or a loose boat it keeps close by holding a tow rope, to attract humanoids seeking to retrieve it.

This monster fares well in the oceanic depths, but it mostly prefers to stay near the coasts, where its favored prey dwell.

Unlike normal octopuses, ozaenae are amphibious and can even walk on land; when out of water, an ozaena can only make four tentacle attacks per round but is capable of taking very long leaps.

An ozaena loots the humans’ fish and mussel farms at night, and since it is attracted to the scent of meat, it even goes a long distance from the sea in order to attack smokehouses and cellars for cured meats; it is very intelligent and vicious, often devising elaborate plans to steal food and lure its prey. Ozaenae are also willing to eat unlucky shipwrecked sailors, dragging them on the bottom of the sea to choke and be devoured.

An ozaena’s head is 5 feet in diameter, while its tentacles are 30 ft. long.
